about: Original pharmacy-career interview questions for Syllo's interview practice (prompts/18). Written for Syllo; not taken from any exam board, regulator or employer. settings: [] = every target; otherwise any of foundation, community, hospital, placement. keyPoints are what a strong answer covers, used to ground AI feedback.

questions.prompt: Why have you chosen a career in pharmacy rather than another healthcare profession?
keyPoints: A genuine, specific reason rather than a generic one
Understanding of what pharmacists actually do day to day
Link to their own experience or strengths
How pharmacy suits them better than nearby roles such as medicine or nursing

questions.prompt: Why do you want to complete your foundation training year with us in particular?
keyPoints: Specific knowledge of the organisation and its training programme
What they hope to learn and the kind of pharmacist they want to become
How the site's patients or services match their interests
What they would contribute in return

questions.prompt: What attracts you to community pharmacy, and what do you think the role will look like in five years?
keyPoints: Interest in direct patient contact and the local community
Awareness of expanding clinical services such as consultations and prescribing
Realistic view of workload and pressures
Where they see themselves contributing

questions.prompt: Why are you interested in hospital pharmacy?
keyPoints: Interest in working on wards with the wider clinical team
Awareness of hospital activities such as medicines reconciliation and clinical screening
Interest in complex or acutely unwell patients
Specific experience or exposure that confirmed the interest

questions.prompt: What do you hope to gain from this placement, and what will you bring to the team?
keyPoints: Clear, realistic learning goals
Willingness to help with routine tasks and learn from them
Relevant skills from study, work or volunteering
Enthusiasm and reliability

questions.prompt: What do you think makes a good pharmacist, and which of those qualities do you already have?
keyPoints: Names several qualities such as accuracy, communication, integrity and empathy
Gives evidence for the qualities they claim
Honest about a quality still being developed
Links qualities to patient care

questions.prompt: Tell me about an achievement you are proud of and what it says about you.
keyPoints: A clear situation and their personal role
Specific actions they took
A measurable or concrete result
Reflection linking it to the role

questions.prompt: Tell me about a recent development in pharmacy or healthcare that interests you and why.
keyPoints: Names a real, relevant development
Explains it accurately in simple terms
Considers the impact on patients and pharmacists
Gives a personal view or how they would engage with it

questions.prompt: Describe a time you disagreed with someone in a team. How did you handle it?
keyPoints: Describes the disagreement fairly without blaming
Listened to the other person's view
Took a constructive action to resolve it
Outcome and what they learned

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time a team member was not pulling their weight. What did you do?
keyPoints: Raised it early and privately
Tried to understand the reason
Focused on the shared goal
Escalated appropriately if needed and reflected on the result

questions.prompt: What role do you usually take in a team? Give an example.
keyPoints: Self-aware description of their usual role
A specific example using situation, task, action and result
Flexibility to take other roles
How their role helped the team succeed

questions.prompt: A doctor disagrees with your recommendation about a patient's medicine on a ward round. How would you approach this?
keyPoints: Stays professional and patient focused
Explains the evidence and reasoning clearly
Listens to the doctor's rationale
Seeks a senior pharmacist or guidance if unresolved and documents the outcome

questions.prompt: How would you build a good working relationship with dispensing staff who have far more experience than you?
keyPoints: Shows respect for their experience
Asks questions and learns from them
Is clear about their own professional responsibilities
Communicates openly and pulls their weight

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you helped a colleague or classmate who was struggling.
keyPoints: Noticed the problem and approached sensitively
Practical support offered
Respected boundaries and involved others if needed
Positive outcome and reflection

questions.prompt: Give an example of a time you led a group towards a goal.
keyPoints: Clear goal and their leadership role
How they organised and motivated others
Handled a difficulty along the way
Concrete result and learning

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you dealt with an upset or angry customer or patient.
keyPoints: Stayed calm and listened
Acknowledged their feelings
Found out the real problem and acted on it
Outcome and what they would repeat or change

questions.prompt: A patient who speaks little English needs advice about a new medicine. How would you make sure they understand?
keyPoints: Uses a professional interpreter or language line rather than relying on family where possible
Simple language, visual aids or translated leaflets
Checks understanding by asking them to explain back
Documents and offers follow-up

questions.prompt: A patient's medicine is out of stock and they are worried. How would you handle the conversation?
keyPoints: Explains honestly and calmly
Checks how urgent it is and the risks of missing doses
Offers practical options such as another pharmacy or contacting the prescriber about an alternative
Agrees a clear plan and follows up

questions.prompt: Describe a time you had to explain something complicated to someone without your background.
keyPoints: Adapted language to the listener
Broke the information into steps or used examples
Checked understanding
Result and what they learned

questions.prompt: Give an example of when listening carefully changed the outcome of a situation.
keyPoints: Specific situation
What they noticed by listening
Action they took as a result
How the outcome improved

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you received critical feedback. How did you respond?
keyPoints: Describes the feedback honestly
Reacted professionally rather than defensively
Took concrete steps to improve
Evidence of improvement

questions.prompt: Your shift is ending and an important task for a patient isn't finished. What do you do?
keyPoints: Recognises the risk to the patient
Hands over clearly to a named colleague with the key details
Documents what has and hasn't been done
Checks the handover was understood

questions.prompt: A friend asks you to give them a prescription-only medicine without a prescription because they have run out. What do you do?
keyPoints: Declines clearly and kindly, without bending the law
Explains the legal and safety reasons
Offers legitimate options such as an emergency supply where appropriate or contacting their prescriber
Maintains professional boundaries with friends

questions.prompt: A patient's relative phones asking what medicines the patient is taking. How do you respond?
keyPoints: Protects confidentiality
Checks identity and whether the patient has consented
Explains why they can't share without consent
Offers ways to help within the rules

questions.prompt: You notice a colleague appears to be under the influence of alcohol at work. What would you do?
keyPoints: Puts patient safety first
Acts promptly and sensitively
Raises it with the responsible pharmacist or manager
Follows workplace policy and supports the colleague

questions.prompt: If a patient asks for a service that conflicts with your personal beliefs, how would you handle it?
keyPoints: Patient care must not be compromised
Refers promptly to another pharmacist or service without judgement
Planned arrangements in advance with the employer
Respectful, non-judgemental communication

questions.prompt: A grateful patient offers you an expensive gift. What do you do?
keyPoints: Recognises the risk to professional boundaries
Politely declines or follows the organisation's gifts policy
Thanks the patient so they don't feel offended
Records or reports it if the policy requires

questions.prompt: A colleague posts a photo online that shows patient information in the background. What would you do?
keyPoints: Recognises a confidentiality breach
Asks the colleague to remove it promptly
Reports it in line with policy
Supports learning to prevent it happening again

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you made a mistake. How did you handle it?
keyPoints: Owns the mistake honestly
Immediate action to limit harm
Told the right people
What they changed so it doesn't happen again

questions.prompt: A patient comes back saying they were given the wrong strength of their medicine. What do you do?
keyPoints: Apologises and checks the patient is safe, including whether doses were taken
Corrects the error and seeks clinical advice if needed
Is open and honest with the patient
Reports it through the incident system and reflects on causes

questions.prompt: While checking a prescription, you spot a potentially serious interaction. What steps do you take?
keyPoints: Assesses how significant the interaction is using reliable references
Considers the patient's history and whether it was intended
Contacts the prescriber with a clear recommendation
Documents the intervention and informs the patient appropriately

questions.prompt: The pharmacy is extremely busy and a manager asks you to check prescriptions faster. How do you respond?
keyPoints: Does not compromise accuracy or safety
Prioritises urgent items
Communicates waiting times honestly to patients
Raises staffing or workload concerns appropriately

questions.prompt: Tell me about a near miss or error you noticed, at work or in study, and what you learned.
keyPoints: Clear description of what nearly happened
How it was noticed and fixed
Reporting or sharing so others learn
A specific change in practice

questions.prompt: What extra checks would you make when handling a high-risk medicine such as an anticoagulant or insulin?
keyPoints: Names relevant checks such as dose, indication, monitoring and recent results
Uses local guidance and up-to-date references
Counsels the patient on safety points
Escalates any doubt before supply

questions.prompt: You are worried that a vulnerable patient may be at risk of harm at home. What would you do?
keyPoints: Takes the concern seriously and listens
Doesn't promise to keep it secret
Follows the safeguarding procedure and speaks to the safeguarding lead
Records facts objectively and acts urgently if there is immediate danger

questions.prompt: You find a discrepancy in the controlled drugs register. What do you do?
keyPoints: Does not ignore or alter records
Investigates likely causes such as recording errors
Informs the responsible pharmacist or manager
Follows the reporting procedure if it can't be resolved

questions.prompt: Two urgent tasks need doing at the same time and you can't do both. How do you decide what to do first?
keyPoints: Prioritises by risk to patients
Gathers the information needed quickly
Delegates or asks for help
Communicates with those waiting and reviews the outcome

questions.prompt: A patient asks a question and you're not sure of the answer. What do you do?
keyPoints: Is honest that they need to check
Uses reliable resources
Asks a senior colleague if needed
Gets back to the patient with a clear answer

questions.prompt: Just before closing, a parent arrives with a prescription for antibiotics for a feverish child. What do you do?
keyPoints: Recognises the clinical urgency
Checks the prescription safely despite time pressure
Counsels on dosing and warning signs
Arranges an alternative supply if it truly can't be dispensed

questions.prompt: On a ward you discover a patient has missed several doses of a time-critical medicine. What do you do?
keyPoints: Treats it as urgent
Finds out why the doses were missed
Works with nursing staff and the prescriber to give the dose or a plan
Reports the incident and helps prevent a repeat

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had too much to do. How did you manage it?
keyPoints: Describes the pressure honestly
Prioritised and planned
Asked for help or renegotiated deadlines
Result and a strategy they still use

questions.prompt: A senior colleague asks you to do something you believe is unsafe. What do you do?
keyPoints: Doesn't proceed with an unsafe action
Raises the concern respectfully with reasons
Seeks another senior view if needed
Follows up and documents

questions.prompt: Describe a time you had to adapt quickly to a change in how things were done.
keyPoints: Describes the change
Positive attitude and practical steps to adapt
Helped others adjust
Result and learning

questions.prompt: Explain to me, as if I were a patient, how to use a new preventer inhaler and why I need to keep using it.
keyPoints: Plain language without jargon
The difference between preventer and reliever and why daily use matters
Key technique points and rinsing the mouth afterwards where relevant
Checks understanding and invites questions

questions.prompt: A patient asks why they can't just stop their antibiotics once they feel better. How would you answer?
keyPoints: Explains the course as prescribed simply
Mentions the infection returning and resistance in plain terms
Gives practical advice about missed doses and side effects
Checks understanding

questions.prompt: A patient has been started on a cholesterol-lowering medicine but doesn't feel ill and isn't sure they need it. How would you talk to them?
keyPoints: Listens to their concerns
Explains prevention of future heart attacks and strokes simply
Gives balanced information about side effects and what to report
Respects their choice and suggests talking to their prescriber

questions.prompt: An older patient is confused about when to take their many medicines. How would you help?
keyPoints: Reviews what they actually take
Simple schedule or chart and support aids where suitable
Involves carers with consent
Considers a medicines review with the prescriber

questions.prompt: Someone asks to buy a strong painkiller over the counter for the third time this week. How do you handle it?
keyPoints: Asks questions sensitively to understand the use
Considers overuse or dependence risks
Gives advice and alternatives
Refers to a GP or support service if appropriate and may decline the sale

questions.prompt: A patient says a medicine is giving them side effects and they want to stop it. What do you say?
keyPoints: Takes the concern seriously and asks about the symptoms
Checks for anything urgent
Explains the risks of stopping suddenly where relevant
Agrees a plan with the prescriber and reporting if appropriate

questions.prompt: How do you check that a patient has really understood the advice you've given them?
keyPoints: Asks them to explain it back in their own words
Uses open questions
Gives written information
Invites them to come back with questions

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time something didn't go to plan. What did you do next?
keyPoints: Honest description of the setback
Practical response rather than giving up
What they learned
How they've applied it since

questions.prompt: How do you manage stress during busy periods?
keyPoints: Specific, healthy strategies
Planning and prioritising
Knowing when to ask for support
An example of it working

questions.prompt: How have you prepared yourself for the registration assessment or your exams so far, and how will you keep that going while working?
keyPoints: Concrete study plan
Use of practice questions and feedback
Balancing work, study and wellbeing
Seeking help on weaker topics

questions.prompt: How will you keep your knowledge up to date throughout your career?
keyPoints: Reflective learning and continuing professional development
Reliable sources and guidelines
Learning from colleagues and feedback
An example of something they learned recently

questions.prompt: What is one area you're working to improve, and what are you doing about it?
keyPoints: A real but manageable area
Specific steps already taken
Evidence of progress
Doesn't present a strength disguised as a weakness

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you started somewhere new. How did you settle in?
keyPoints: Describes the new environment
Proactive steps such as asking questions and learning routines
Built relationships
How quickly they became effective

questions.prompt: Tell me about a patient or customer interaction that changed how you work.
keyPoints: Specific interaction described with respect and without identifying details
What they realised
What they now do differently
Impact on later patients
